# From a code change onto existing specs

After a Cursor plugin install, the short command loop is [plugins/crav1/README.md](../plugins/crav1/README.md).

Use this when **specs already exist** under `docs/specs/` and a **code change already landed** without a spec, plan, or build.

It is not [from the repos](from-existing-to-specs-repos-only.md) (`$crav1-existing-to-specs`), which reads the repos the user named and writes one architecture spec.

A not-started spec (match status `not in the code`, or a thin spec) can keep taking information until planning. Adding what the change does does not start planning and does not write `plan.md` or `tasks.md`.

## First prompt

```text
$crav1-add-to-spec

The specs already exist. Sort this change onto them.
Do not write code. Do not plan.
```

## Steps

| Phase | You | Agent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Change | Named a commit, a range, or the branch diff, or pick from the options | Options only when the change was not named. Recent commits, or the branch diff. Does not ask for a typed hash |
| Specs | — | Reads `docs/specs/<slug>/` (skips `_template`). Does not ask for a slug |
| Sort | Confirm or edit the three piles | Belongs to this spec, already described there, or fits none of them. Stops |
| Write | — | Quotes what the change does into the matching `spec.md` files. Labels what is new versus what was already there. Inferred stays inferred. Does not invent acceptance, architecture, or tasks |
| Impact | If other files are affected, pick apply or leave them alone | Reads `docs/system/` and the other specs. Lists each proposed edit in one line. Does not edit those files until apply |
| Stop | Glance, then `$crav1-finalize-commit` only if those spec edits should be committed | Does not plan, implement, or commit |

No spec folders under `docs/specs/` (other than `_template`): the command stops and points at `$crav1-existing-to-specs`.

The card is `yes (Recommended)` to write it as shown, or typed changes on that card's free-text answer. It does not say `table above` unless that table is in the reply.

## What gets written

The matching `docs/specs/<slug>/spec.md` files, for what the change does that was not already described there.

Other `docs/system/` files and other specs change only when apply is picked.

No `plan.md`. No `tasks.md`. A missing `docs/system/` is not seeded here. A missing `glossary.md` is a gap fill only when `docs/system/` already exists. A meaning the change does not state is `to be researched`. When `docs/system/` already exists, that same pass adds what is new to the short description, the diagram, and how the parts connect. A whole-repo read sets that repo's `Synced at` line in `repos.md`. A one-slice read writes `Synced at: <repo> <branch>@<short sha>, <date>` on that slice's `spec.md` and does not touch the `repos.md` section.

## One spec, several branches (1.64.0)

In this example the specs live in `orders-specs`, the code in the sibling checkout `../orders-api`, whose default branch is `main` but whose work merges into `develop`. Three branches carry the `orders` spec: `feature/orders-openapi` (1 commit), `feat/orders-retry` (2) and `feature/orders-export` (3).

```text
$crav1-add-to-spec code-change orders-api feature/orders-openapi
```

- **Which checkout.** `orders-api` is read from `../orders-api`, read-only. When it isn't there, the kit asks for the path (options only). A headless run stops with `No checkout found for orders-api. Name its path.`
- **Fork point.** The branch diff starts where the branch split off, not at `main`: `Branch diff of feature/orders-openapi from develop (split at 00344be): 1 commit.` Measured from `main` it would be every commit on develop too. The report shows the age of each remote copy it read; nothing is fetched.
- **Branch list.** A one-slice read of a work branch also adds it to the spec's Match `Branch:` list, one line per branch in sorted place, for example `- Branch: orders-api feat/orders-retry` and, on the next line, `- Branch: orders-api feature/orders-openapi`. Base branches are never added, and existing entries and their markers stay.
- **Merges into.** Because the parent is `develop`, not the default branch, the kit asks once: `Work in orders-api merges into develop. Record that in repos.md?` A yes writes `develop` in the `Merges into` column. A headless run doesn't ask and writes nothing.
- **Synced at.** The spec gains one line per branch: `Synced at: orders-api feat/orders-retry@155b5c4, 2026-10-19` and `Synced at: orders-api feature/orders-openapi@85d4561, 2026-10-19`, one line each. A new read of a branch replaces only that line.
- **No double import.** The note lists the commits it imported: `commits: [85d4561]`. Running the same branch again says `already imported`. A rebased or cherry-picked copy of an imported commit is `same change as <sha> in <note>` (matched by `git patch-id`). Only new commits are imported. When the branch was force-pushed since the last read, the run says `branch rewritten since last read` and carries on. A squash merge is recognised only through a merged PR on GitHub (`gh`) or Azure DevOps (`az`); anywhere else it is listed as `may already be in <note>` for you to keep or drop.
- **One note, several specs.** When the change feeds two specs, one note serves both (`used_by` lists both).

`$crav1-tighten-spec`, `$crav1-plan-from-spec`, `$crav1-help status`, `$crav1-tasks-ready-to-build`, `$crav1-verify-build-against-spec`, `$crav1-open-pr` and `$crav1-merge-pr` then read all three branches. The other skills that write a slice `Synced at` line (`$crav1-spark-to-spec`, `$crav1-ideas-to-spec`, `$crav1-bundle-to-specs`, `$crav1-refresh-system-notes`) keep the other branches' entries too, and `$crav1-existing-to-specs` templates carry the `Merges into` column.

## From a pull request (1.65.0)

A code change can be a pull request: `$crav1-add-to-spec code-change orders-api PR 71`, or its URL. The pull request's title and description are saved as the PR note (`docs/notes/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD-pr-orders-api-71.md`, by its created date, `kind: pull request`), or reused when it exists, after the personal-data and secrets check. The code-change note links it with `pr_note:`, and a spec point taken from the description gets `Full source:` with the PR note's path.

Given a branch instead, it also writes the PR note when a signed-in `gh` or `az` host shows exactly one pull request for that branch. Otherwise it writes none and says why in one line, for example `no PR note: 2 PRs for feat/orders-retry; name one as PR <n>`. It never asks, and never stops because of it.

## Every open branch: `branches` (1.79.0)

`$crav1-add-to-spec branches`, or `$crav1-add-to-spec orders-api branches` for a repo in `repos.md`, lists every branch that is not merged into its base and has commits not read yet, from the local branches and the remote-tracking copies already on disk. It never fetches.

```
feat/orders-retry      3 new, last 2026-10-20, remote: 2 days
feat/orders-export     1 new, last 2026-06-02, remote: 4 months, stale (no commits since 2026-06-02)
```

`branches-all` and `branches-skip-stale` answer it up front. The kit never deletes, pushes or fetches.

## A PR ref alone, and `all` (1.76.0)

`$crav1-add-to-spec pr71` (also `pr 71`, `#71`, or `pr orders-api 71`) is the same code change; the `code-change` word is not needed.

`$crav1-add-to-spec pr71 all` also checks for new commits and appends `## PR updates as of <date>` to the PR note: the description when it changed, then one heading per thread, such as `### src/Orders/Retry.cs:42 (resolved)` or `### Conversation (open)`, each comment with its author as the host shows it, the date and the text, replies nested. A later `all` adds only new or edited comments and one line per resolved or reopened thread. A comment that answers an open question is linked as `Answered:`; a decision becomes an open question.

## After

```text
Next: $crav1-tighten-spec <slug>, because the new information is not tightened yet.
Uncommitted: 1 file; commit with $crav1-finalize-commit when ready.
```
